correctness.rationale: Exact pairwise XOR-difference criterion, explicit completeness of 2^15 anchored nonempty teams by XOR translation, and an independently implemented full 65,535-team agreement-based enumeration verify 221 profiles. Tracking every minimal team size gives distribution (1,15,35,67,95,8) and maximum six; direct 24-permutation orbit computation gives 32 orbits, independently checked by Burnside fixed counts 221,55,25,14,5. Concrete two six-world witnesses and classification of their four-member orbits are asserted in the standalone checker. All 32,768 candidate Moore families are separately checked giving 2,480. Code was run from the public artifact path and completed successfully; no infinite proof is inferred from finite sampling, because the claim is an exhaustively bounded finite classification.

originality.rationale: The exact restricted finite statement (221 named binary team closure profiles, 32 attribute-renaming types, complete minimal-world histogram, and two size-six exceptional classes) is not stated nor implied by the inspected primary literature. General Armstrong existence and bounds allow arbitrary domains; Beeri et al. 1984, Theorem 6.10 supplies an existential obstruction to binary representability but not its exact four-attribute classification. Ciardelli–Conti 2026 develops calculus and supervenience semantics, not the finite classification. The 2,480 unrestricted Moore-family count is known and is not claimed as new. Multiple exact source/alias queries in current public research records and published literature found no covering result. Genuine risk remains from unindexed finite database-dependence enumerations.

value.rationale: The complete binary-realizability subset of 221 among 2,480 abstract four-attribute closure theories is a natural finite expressive invariant for modal global supervenience and Armstrong database dependence. The sharp six-world cutoff and exactly two exceptional renaming types solve a concrete optimal representation-size question; the former is the first size beyond n+1 for n<=4, verified by lower-arity censuses. This matters for constructing and separating small models of dependence logics and is not a textbook renaming of the known 2,480 count or of Armstrong existence.
